answer: Each bonded identity commits collateral to escrow, and verifiable correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities triggers a pooled penalty proportional to k², not k. Detection also applies a swarm-size multiplier m^k, where m>1, to capital loss; asymmetric depreciation makes slashed collateral harder to replace. Splitting control across aliases therefore raises exposure rather than diluting it. A reef of nominally separate nodes, across a karst-like topology or prism of operators, cannot evade linkage when signed actions share evidence.
